description: 1400-COMPUTE-FEES IS INVOKED AND PROVABLY CHANGES NOTHING - the AFFIRMATIVE half of gate G26, asserted by an EXHAUSTIVE CLOSED INVENTORY rather than by any single expected value. case13 is the negative half: there DIS-INT-RATE is 0.00, the guard at :214 is false and the stub is never reached at all. Here the rate is 15.00, so :216 PERFORM 1400-COMPUTE-FEES genuinely EXECUTES, once, immediately after :215 PERFORM 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST and inside the same IF. The whole value of this case is its COMPLETENESS, because absence of an assertion is not an assertion of absence: a case that merely omitted any mention of fees would prove nothing whatever. What is asserted instead is every artefact the run produced, closed on all sides, so a fee artefact of any kind would appear as a SURPLUS and be reported by parity.FieldDiffer as a difference. WHAT THE STUB IS, IN FULL. app/cbl/CBACT04C.cbl:518-520 is three lines - the paragraph header, the comment '* To be implemented', and EXIT. It contains no COMPUTE, no MOVE, no WRITE, no DISPLAY and no PERFORM: ZERO statements. It touches no field of TRAN-RECORD, no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD, no counter and no file. Its Java counterpart, account.AccountInterestCalcJob.computeFees(), is an intentionally empty method invoked from exactly the :216 position, and IT MUST REMAIN A NO-OP. This is a deliberately preserved unimplemented stub, not an oversight waiting to be filled in: implementing fee logic would be a new feature, the plan prohibits new features outright because this is a like-for-like language migration with no changed business rules, and practice B5 requires dead code be preserved rather than tidied, deleted or completed. THE INVENTORY IS CLOSED BECAUSE THE WRITE SURFACE IS ENUMERABLE (practice B8). This program can write to exactly TWO datasets and no others. (1) The generated-transaction output, via WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC FROM TRAN-RECORD at :500. (2) The account master, via REWRITE FD-ACCTFILE-REC FROM ACCOUNT-RECORD at :356. Everything else it opens is opened INPUT - TCATBALF at :236, XREF-FILE at :254 and DISCGRP-FILE at :272 - and none of the three has a WRITE or a REWRITE anywhere in the program. Both writable datasets are inventoried below to the byte, which is what makes 'a fee changed nothing' a proof rather than an absence of evidence: there is nowhere else for a fee to hide. A NOTE ON THE MEMBER NAMES FIRST (practice B4). The brief for this case asks for a member called expectedRecords. parity.ParityCase declares no such member and every type in it is annotated @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = false), so that name is not merely unconventional here, it is unloadable - it would fail at load time rather than bind to nothing, which is the safer of the two failures but a failure all the same. The three real members are used instead, exactly as every other case in this folder uses them: expectedWrites for what the unit wrote and in what order, expectedFinalState for what each dataset holds afterwards, and expectedDatasets for the one thing neither row list can state - that a dataset was opened and holds exactly N rows. The correction is recorded rather than applied silently. (A) THE GENERATED-TRANSACTION OUTPUT HOLDS EXACTLY ONE RECORD. It is pinned twice over: as all FOURTEEN CVTRA05Y fields in an ordered field-to-value map in copybook declaration order, because FieldDiffer compares field by field and never as one opaque string (gate G17); and as the complete 350-byte image, which is what proves the total width and therefore that the trailing FILLER X(20) was emitted as spaces rather than dropped or zero-filled (gate G21). 350 is CVTRA05Y's declared width and app/jcl/INTCALC.jcl:39's RECFM=F,LRECL=350 exactly (gates G19, G20). SYSTRAN is additionally pinned on the WRITES channel at rowCount 1 and recordLength 350, so the count is asserted independently of the row: an inventory that pinned one row but left the count unstated could not distinguish one record from that record plus a second nobody looked at. THE FOURTEEN FIELDS ARE THE FIRST HALF OF THE G26 ARGUMENT. Every field is accounted for and NOT ONE OF THEM IS A FEE. CVTRA05Y declares no fee field at all, and TRAN-CAT-CD is the constant 0005 on every record this program writes - :483 moves the literal '05' unconditionally - so there is no second category value under which a fee transaction could be distinguished. A fee could therefore only manifest as a SECOND record in this dataset, and this case asserts there is exactly one. Field by field: TRAN-ID is 2022071800000001, because ADD 1 TO WS-TRANID-SUFFIX at :474 runs BEFORE the STRING at :476-480 and WS-TRANID-SUFFIX is PIC 9(06) VALUE 0, so the first identifier ends 000001 and never 000000, with PARM-DATE contributing the ten characters of INTCALC.jcl:22 PARM='2022071800' verbatim as character data for an exact 10+6=16 byte fit. TRAN-CAT-CD is 0005 and not '05  ', because :483 moves an alphanumeric literal into a PIC 9(04) numeric-display receiver, which de-edits to the integer 5 and stores right-aligned and zero-filled; getting that wrong shifts bytes 19-22 and cascades into all 331 that follow. TRAN-SOURCE is 'System' plus FOUR trailing spaces, ten bytes. TRAN-DESC is 24 composed bytes then a 76-byte tail of spaces: the literal 'Int. for a/c ' is thirteen characters including its trailing space, ACCT-ID contributes 00000000050, and the STRING at :485-489 does not blank the remainder of its receiver, which common.FixedWidthCodec has space-initialised. TRAN-MERCHANT-ID is nine zeros from MOVE 0 into PIC 9(09), and the three merchant text spans are 50, 50 and 10 spaces from :492-494. TRAN-CARD-NUM is 0500024453765740, resolved through the alternate index at :495 from the row whose XREF-ACCT-ID at 1-based bytes 26-36 reads 00000000050 - matched on the field, never on position, because cardxref.txt is ordered by CARD NUMBER and positional correspondence to an account does not hold. That row happens to be zero-based row 0. THE ARITHMETIC, AND WHY IT IS DELIBERATELY UNINTERESTING (gates G23, G24, G25, G28). COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 at :464-465 carries NO ROUNDED - the keyword appears zero times in all 28 programs - and its receiver is WS-MONTHLY-INT PIC S9(09)V99 at :168, so the policy is BigDecimal at scale 2 with RoundingMode.DOWN and never HALF_UP or HALF_EVEN. 492.00 x 15.00 = 7380.0000, divided by 1200 = 6.1500 EXACTLY, which at scale 2 is 6.15. That quotient is exact, so this case is NOT a rounding discriminator: 6.15 is the answer under DOWN, HALF_UP, HALF_EVEN, CEILING and FLOOR alike, all five checked. The clean value was chosen on purpose, so that the inventory assertion is not entangled with a rounding argument - that job belongs to case06, case07 and case08, and a case cannot make two arguments cleanly at once. The zoned image is 0000000061E: eleven bytes for S9(09)V99, digit string 00000000615, and E is the positive overpunch of a low-order 5. ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT TO WS-TOTAL-INT at :467 then leaves WS-TOTAL-INT at 6.15 - a value which, as (B) explains, is never applied anywhere. (B) THE ACCOUNT MASTER RECEIVES EXACTLY ZERO REWRITES, AND ALL FIFTY ROWS PROVE IT. ACCTFILE carries no entry in expectedWrites, and all fifty of its rows appear in expectedFinalState byte-identical to their seed. That pair IS the assertion 'no REWRITE happened', not an omission, and pinning the whole master rather than only account 50 is what makes it strong: a fee reaching ANY account row, not merely the one this run read, would be reported. Two INDEPENDENT reasons, stated separately because they fail independently (practice B1). FIRST, control flow: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT is reached from :196 only on an account break where WS-FIRST-TIME is NOT 'Y', and with a single input record this break IS the first, so :195 routes to :198 and merely flips the flag. Its only other call site is the ELSE at :219-220, which is UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE: the enclosing PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' at :188 makes the IF END-OF-FILE = 'N' at :189 always true, so the last - and here only - account group is never flushed to the master and the 6.15 in WS-TOTAL-INT is silently discarded at GOBACK. That is the legacy behaviour and practice B5 forbids 'fixing' it; a run that added an end-of-file flush would rewrite account 50 to 498.15 and fail this case. SECOND, the field list: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT at :350-370 is the ONLY place this program writes to the account master, and it names exactly three fields - ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL at :352, MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT at :353 and MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT at :354 - before the REWRITE at :356. So EVEN HAD A REWRITE OCCURRED, no fee could have reached the account record: there is no field for one to land in. That closes the second and last channel through which a fee could ever become observable. AND A THIRD CORRECTION, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED (practice B4). The brief asks for the zero rewrites to be stated as an ACCTFILE row count of zero. On the WRITES channel that assertion is not available for this program and would INVERT the case: CBACT04CParityTest reports only SYSTRAN on the writes channel, and FieldDiffer raises a MISSING_DATASET difference for a dataset-level expectation naming a channel the fingerprint does not carry - so an ACCTFILE/WRITES/0 entry would fail a run that behaved perfectly. The zero is therefore asserted where it is observable: absent from expectedWrites, unchanged across all fifty rows of expectedFinalState, and counted there at exactly 50 rows of 300 bytes. (C) NO OTHER DATASET IS WRITTEN, AND EACH IS PINNED WHOLE. TCATBALF, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1 and DISCGRP are all opened INPUT and none is ever written; all four appear in expectedFinalState identical to their seeds and are counted in expectedDatasets - 1 row of 50, 50 of 50, 50 of 50 and 51 of 50 respectively. With SYSTRAN's single row and ACCTFILE's fifty untouched rows that is 203 pinned records across six datasets, and every dataset this program opens is among them. There is no fourth category of output left unasserted. MESSAGES: EXACTLY FIVE LINES, DECLARED EXHAUSTIVE (practice B1). In emission order: the :181 banner; the raw 50-byte DISPLAY TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD at :193, reproducing the seeded row byte for byte at its full width; 'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING' at :418; 'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE' at :419; and the :230 banner. FIVE, AND A SIXTH LINE OF ANY KIND IS A FAILURE. 1400-COMPUTE-FEES contributes NO message, because it contains no DISPLAY at all - which is the third and last way a fee could have been observable, and it is closed by the count. WS-RECORD-COUNT is incremented at :192 but never displayed anywhere in the program, so it contributes nothing either. Absent and deliberately so: 'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE' at :431 and 'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP' at :455, because '23' is tolerated at :422 and the retry succeeds; 'ERROR WRITING TRANSACTION RECORD' at :510 and 'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE' at :365, because both I/O paths return '00'; 'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: ' at :375 and :397, because both keyed reads found their record; and 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at :629 with its rendered FILE STATUS line, because nothing here reaches 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. expectedReturnCode is 0 accordingly. THE DISCLOSURE-GROUP MISS IS REAL, AND THE GROUP-ID CLAIM IN THE BRIEF IS WRONG (practice B4). :210-212 build the lookup key from ACCT-GROUP-ID, TRANCAT-CD and TRANCAT-TYPE-CD. Read mechanically against app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, ACCT-GROUP-ID occupies 1-based bytes 113-122 and is TEN SPACES for account 50 - and, checked exhaustively, for ALL FIFTY rows of acctdata.txt. The A000000000 that a reader might mistake for it is ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at bytes 103-112, one field earlier. So the key is ten spaces plus '01' plus '0001', which is present in no row of discgrp.txt - the file holds exactly three key blocks, A000000000, 'DEFAULT   ' and 'ZEROAPR   ' - the READ at :416 misses with FILE STATUS '23', the INVALID KEY arm at :417-419 emits the two fallback lines, '23' is tolerated at :422, and :436-438 moves 'DEFAULT' into the key and retries through 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE, which succeeds with '00'. Gate G47's '23'-then-retry outcome, exercised end to end. THE KEY-WIDTH TRAP, MEASURED (practice B11). app/cpy/CVTRA02Y.cpy declares DIS-GROUP-KEY as X(10) + X(02) + 9(04) = SIXTEEN bytes, so DIS-INT-RATE S9(04)V99 occupies 1-based bytes 17-22, which on the row 'DEFAULT   01000100150{' plus its 28-byte trailing span reads 00150{ = 15.00. The genuinely SEVENTEEN-byte key is CVTRA01Y's TRAN-CAT-KEY, and because both records total 50 bytes the slip is invisible by width alone. Read at 18-23 instead, this row yields 0150{0 - an overpunch stranded mid-span - which would corrupt the rate and every byte of TRAN-AMT with it. The rate was read at 17-22. DETERMINISM, AND A SECOND CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF (practices B7, B4). TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS are this program's only wall-clock values; Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP at :613-626 composes DB2-FORMAT-TS as YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.mm0000 to exactly 26 bytes and :497-498 move the identical value into both, so no 'now' is ever captured. The brief asks for them to be pinned at 2022-07-18-00.00.00.000000; that value is NOT REACHABLE. ParityCase publishes pinnedClock on ScreenRequest alone and forbids a ScreenRequest on a BATCH_JOB outright, so a batch case cannot pin a clock of its own; what applies instead is ParityHarness.DEFAULT_PINNED_CLOCK, which exists for exactly this reason and is fixed at 2022-07-19T23:12:34, rendering as the 26-byte 2022-07-19-23.12.34.000000 - the value every other shipped case in this folder pins. That instant is traceable rather than arbitrary: the repository-wide source footer reads 'Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19'. The determinism the brief asked for is fully preserved and only the unreachable literal is corrected, in the open. Determinism matters more than usual here: an inventory assertion is only meaningful if it is reproducible, and a captured wall-clock value would make the single expected record fail on every run, masking the very surplus-detection this case is built to perform. PROVENANCE OF THE ONE MODIFIED SPAN, DISCLOSED IN FULL (practice B12). Exactly one span is not fixture-verbatim, and it is not dressed up as though it were. All FIFTY rows of app/data/ASCII/tcatbal.txt carry TRAN-CAT-BAL 0000000000{ - one distinct value, checked exhaustively - so the shipped fixture cannot reach the rate-bearing path at all: at a balance of 0.00 the computed interest is 0.00 whatever the rate, the fees stub would still be invoked but the record it accompanies would carry a zero amount, and the inventory would be far weaker. The row seeded into TCATBALF is therefore account 00000000050's OWN fixture row - its 17-byte key 00000000050 + '01' + '0001' and its 22-byte trailing span, both verbatim - with the balance replaced by 0000004920{, which is 492.00 at CVTRA01Y's declared S9(09)V99 scale. That figure is NOT invented: it is account 50's real ACCT-CURR-BAL in acctdata.txt, the twelve bytes 00000004920{, so the amount is fixture-derived even though the row is modified. ACCTFILE, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1 and DISCGRP are seeded from their fixtures entirely UNMODIFIED - all 50, 50, 50 and 51 rows - and no override of any kind is applied to them: this case asserts an inventory, not a balance delta, so it has no reason to alter an account. WIDTHS, SEEDS AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE PAD (gates G16, G19, G21, G45). Each ACCTFILE image is 300 bytes, CVACT01Y's declared width, and its trailing FILLER X(178) is emitted as 178 spaces - a total that fails immediately if FILLER is dropped or zero-filled, which is how gate G21 is enforced. The seeded TCATBALF row and the displayed line are each exactly 50 bytes, CVTRA01Y's width; each DISCGRP row is 50, CVTRA02Y's. Each cross-reference row is CVACT03Y's 50 bytes in expectedFinalState and 36 in the fixture: the shipped cardxref.txt is 36 bytes per record because it omits CVACT03Y's trailing FILLER X(14), the fixture is NEVER edited and NEVER pre-padded here, and the 14 spaces are supplied once, at seed time, by the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation, which parity.FieldDiffer owns (risk R-F). XREFFILE and XREFFIL1 are seeded from the SAME fifty rows because XREFFIL1 is an alternate-index PATH over the same base cluster and not a second dataset; INTCALC.jcl:29-32 opens both in one step, which is the shape gate G45 is about, and neither is mutated. SYSTRAN is output only and is not seeded. EXPLICIT ADDRESSING AND EXPLICIT BYTES (practice B8). Every dataset is addressed by its carddemo.datasets BINDING KEY - TCATBALF, ACCTFILE, XREFFILE, XREFFIL1, DISCGRP and the SYSTRAN output - and never by a fully-qualified mainframe dataset name; no such name appears anywhere in this file, including in this prose, so gate G46 is structural here rather than a matter of care, and ParityCase's binding-key pattern could not accept a dotted name in any event. Note that INTCALC.jcl:37-41 spells the output DD TRANSACT while pointing it at SYSTRAN(+1); the rows land in the sequential output, so SYSTRAN is the key, and the transaction master that shares those eight characters is untouched by this program. Every rowIndex is ZERO-BASED - a write position in expectedWrites and a row position within the dataset in expectedFinalState - and rows are pinned in stored-image ascending order, which for these three already-ascending fixtures is file order. Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching app/data/ASCII, and never a platform default. REFERENCE INPUTS ARE UNTOUCHED (practice B3). The single override lives inside this JSON. Not one byte of app/cbl, app/cpy, app/jcl or app/data was changed to write this case: tcatbal.txt still carries fifty zero balances, acctdata.txt still leaves ACCT-GROUP-ID blank, discgrp.txt is unmodified and cardxref.txt is still 36 bytes per record. HOW THE UNIT IS REACHED (gate G51): account.AccountInterestCalcJob is invoked at step level through calculateInterest, with no HTTP layer, no JobLauncher, no job repository and no step executor between the assertion and the code. PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the COBOL paragraphs cross-checked against the CVTRA05Y, CVTRA01Y, CVTRA02Y, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts, the INTCALC.jcl DD and PARM contract, and the real ASCII fixtures. Nothing was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment. GOVERNING RULES: review_rules returns the single line 'No user rules provided.' - that is the entire document. No rule is invented and its absence is not treated as permission to lower the bar; the plan's best-practice substitutes bind instead, and the ones this case turns on are named inline above - B1 for the argued-zero rewrite expectation and the exhaustive message list, B3, B4 for the three recorded corrections, B5 as this case's primary obligation, B7, B8, B11 and B12. GATES OWNED: G15, G16, G17, G18, G19, G20, G21, G23, G24, G25, G26, G28, G45, G46, G47 and G51.
